policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV text reads the name as 'Zabbud', which renders the ketiv וזבוד; the qere וְזַכּ֑וּר would be 'Zaccur', and the ASV's textual_variant note 'Another reading is, Zaccur' places the qere in the margin, confirming the text follows the ketiv.

ASV text 'And I sent them forth' renders the ketiv ואוצאה (hiphil of יצא, 'brought/sent out'); the qere וָאֲצַוֶּ֤ה ('I commanded') is what the textual_variant note 'Another reading is, I gave them commandment' relegates to the margin.

ASV 'the Nethinim' transliterates the qere form הַנְּתִינִים֙ (the proper class-name Nethinim); the ketiv הנתונים would be the passive participle 'those given/appointed' and could not yield the transliteration. The verse's textual_variant note concerns the 'sent forth/commanded' unit, not this one.

Qere וָאֶשְׁקֳלָ֣ה and ketiv ואשקולה differ only in plene spelling of the same form 'and I weighed'; ASV 'and weighed' renders either identically and no note is mapped to the unit, so the base qere fallback carries the projection.
